column2: Byzantine–Sasanian War of 602–628: The Sasanian Empire declared war on Byzantium.
column3: Augustus Phocas dedicated the Column of Phocas in the Roman Forum.
column4: Siege of Constantinople (626): Sasanian and Avar forces laid siege to Constantinople.
column5: Muslim conquest of the Levant: A Rashidun army departed Medina for the Levant.
column6: Muslim conquest of Egypt: A Rashidun force laid siege to Pelusium.
column7: The legions of the East Roman army were reorganized into themes.
column8: Siege of Alexandria (641): Byzantine authorities in the Egyptian capital Alexandria surrendered to the besieging Rashidun army.
column9: Brothers Perctarit and Godepert share the ruling power of King of the Lombards.
column11: Battle of Carthage (698): An Umayyad siege and blockade of Carthage forced the retreat of Byzantine forces. The city was conquered and destroyed.
